A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same WildFeedback research. Their text, tables, figures, and complete appendices are readable and support reliable matching across additions, moves, and renumbering.

before.justification: v3 reports original model evaluations in Table 3 and Figures 2–3, plus human validation of feedback classification and checklist-guided evaluation in Appendices B–C.

after.justification: v4 retains these original experiments and additionally reports satisfaction and dissatisfaction category distributions in Section 5.2 and Appendix B.2.

M1.justification: Feedback identification, preference-pair construction, on-policy filtering, SFT/DPO training, and checklist-guided judging remain unchanged. The full prompts in Appendix A are also retained.

E1.justification: Training and evaluation retain the same WildChat/WildFeedback and UltraFeedback coverage, AlpacaEval 2, Arena-Hard, and MT-Bench. HelpSteer2 is added only to the descriptive dataset-statistics table; no training or evaluation using it is reported.

E2.justification: Table 3 and Figure 3 retain the same instruction-tuned and UltraFeedback GPT-4/on-policy comparators for Phi 3, LLaMA 3, and Qwen 2. HelpSteer2 is not added as an evaluated comparison method.

E3.justification: Training budgets, benchmark metrics and judges, the 540-sample held-out evaluation, and human-validation sample sizes remain unchanged. Rubric-category selection already appears in v3 Figure 4, retained as v4 Figure 5; the new distribution reporting does not establish a changed annotation task.

E4.justification: Section 5.2 and Appendix B.2 add a focused analysis of which feedback categories account for satisfaction and dissatisfaction, including a human-versus-GPT-4o comparison of factual-error frequencies. Existing checklist comparisons and hyperparameter observations are retained.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run uncertainty, confidence intervals, or significance tests. Human annotation counts and agreement-reporting practices are unchanged; the added category percentages are descriptive results.

E6.justification: New Tables 6–7 report category frequencies, including Revision at 50.36%, Factual Errors at 18.55%, and Praise at 30.39%. Appendix B.2 also reports a 20.32% GPT-4o factual-error share. Existing benchmark scores, checklist results, and human-agreement values are unchanged.

T1.justification: No theoretical results, proofs, or substantive mathematical revisions are introduced. The existing SAT/DSAT rubric definitions remain unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract and introduction retain the main contributions. The conclusion replaces the assertion that the method aligns diverse human values and enhances user satisfaction with an aspiration to encourage learning from real-world interactions, modestly softening its closing claim.

C2.justification: New discussion interprets dissatisfaction as concentrated in revision and factuality issues, while satisfaction spans more varied positive signals. Limitations now explicitly mentions noisy feedback and changes dissatisfied users being 'twice as likely' to provide feedback to 'more likely,' retaining the underlying selection-bias concern.

D1.justification: Appendix B.2 explicitly explains the use of rubric-based annotation justifications, and Tables 6–7 specify that their distributions exclude N/A. Core prompts, training hyperparameters, GPU times, dataset access, and privacy-processing information remain unchanged.

R1.justification: Related Work adds citations to Shi et al. (2026), Buening et al. (2026), Pan et al. (2025), and Song et al. (2025). Table 2 adds HelpSteer2 and Wang et al. (2024). These extend the literature coverage without substantially revising the existing research positioning.

P1.justification: v4 adds subsections 5.1–5.2 and subheadings within Appendix B.2, rewrites the limitations and concluding sentence, and adds acknowledgments and Appendix F on manuscript LLM use. Most existing prose and document organization are retained.

P2.justification: v4 adds the two-panel distribution chart in Figure 4, category Tables 6–7, and a HelpSteer2 row in Table 2. Existing appendix tables and screenshots are reflowed and renumbered; the original experimental plots and benchmark-table structure remain unchanged.

improvement.justification: Section 5.2, Figure 4, and Appendix B.2 make the feedback composition more interpretable through category frequencies and the human/GPT-4o factual-error comparison, which v3 lacked. The softened conclusion also improves claim calibration. These provide a limited overall gain in transparency and interpretation; the core experimental evidence and uncertainty reporting remain unchanged.
